---
title: "Install iblatlas"
---

## Install

```bash
pip install iblatlas
```

**Python 3.10 or newer** is required.

This pulls in `ONE-api`, `iblutil`, `pynrrd`, `numpy`, `matplotlib` and `scipy`.

## Configure ONE

`ONE-api` is a hard dependency, not an optional one, and it must be **configured** as well as
installed — the atlas cache directory is derived from ONE's `CACHE_DIR` parameter.

This applies even if you only want anatomy and will never touch IBL experimental data. If
`AllenAtlas()` fails on a fresh machine, an unconfigured ONE is the first thing to check. See
[Data downloads and caching](../explanation/data-downloads-and-caching.qmd).

## First use downloads several gigabytes

```python
from iblatlas.atlas import AllenAtlas

ba = AllenAtlas()   # first call downloads the atlas volume
```

The download happens once per resolution and is cached; later calls read from disk. Build one
atlas object and pass it around rather than constructing one repeatedly — most functions that
need an atlas accept it as an argument.

The default resolution is 25 µm. The 10 µm volume is considerably larger; take the default
unless you need the detail.

## The `gui` extra

```bash
pip install "iblatlas[gui]"
```

This adds `pyqt5`, `qtpy` and `iblqt`, and provides an `atlas` command. The GUI is not covered
by this documentation yet.
